activeExperiments.hypothesis: Audit of 2,569 published articles shows OIC-tagged stories (10% of corpus) have a median regional-source share of 20% and only 51.4% include ≥1 regional outlet. The selector currently treats regional outlets as a soft tiebreaker only, so when feed clustering doesn't bundle a regional outlet into a story's cluster, the regional voice gets dropped. Adding an explicit selection-criteria item plus an internal-verification check that requires regional carry-through for OIC-tagged stories — drawing from the broader feed, not just the cluster — should raise ≥1 regional-source coverage on OIC stories from 51.4% to ≥80% over the 7-day window without dropping throughput. Token-neutral: prompt change only, no extra NewsAPI calls.
activeExperiments.oldValue: Muslim-world outlets listed under reader-aligned-sources tiebreaker only
activeExperiments.newValue: Explicit OIC-region carry-through rule + internal-verification check, with named recognized outlets per OIC country

history.hypothesis: Audit on 2026-05-02 found 31 niche-only articles shipped over 6 weeks that recapped events major outlets had broken 2-10 days earlier. Slug-fuzzy was missing them because niche outlets reword headlines and slug truncation drops endings. Adding a layer-4 recap rule (title-word overlap ≥3 words, ≥0.55 ratio, niche-only stories only, 14-day lookback against article titles + ledger labels) should catch the bulk of these without raising fabrication or dropping legitimate breaking news.
history.oldValue: 3 layers: exact slug, eventUri, fuzzy slug
history.newValue: + layer 4: recap (niche-only, titleWords overlap ≥0.55 / ≥3 words, 14d lookback)
history.targetMetric: niche-source recap articles caught per week
history.notes: Retroactive backtest via scripts/autoresearch/replay-recap-dedup.js (mode=published) over the 2026-03-21 → 2026-05-01 pre-launch window: 22 niche-only articles deterministically caught by the recap rule across 742 niche-only publishes (~3.7/week). Source concentration is heavy: Drop Site News 9 (40%), New Lines 3, Salaam Gateway 2, The Record 2 — top 4 outlets cover 73% of value. ~14 of 22 are clean recaps (Disney/OpenAI, Tadamon arrest, Drift exploit, Australia ban, Bint Jbeil, etc.); ~7 are conflict-cluster matches (Israel-Lebanon recurring strikes treated as recaps — explicitly pinned in test fixture as KNOWN_RECAPS, intentional aggressiveness); ~1 borderline false-positive (Salaam Gateway Iran/Gulf tourism vs Iran-UAE aluminium strike). 7 of the 14 KNOWN_RECAPS pins fall inside this window and were all caught. Post-launch (2026-05-02 → 2026-05-09): 106 niche-only publishes, 1 clear false negative (Phys.org Venter recap of 2026-04-30 break). Cost: zero — deterministic, no LLM. Trade-off: rule is intentionally aggressive on conflict-cluster recaps; if that becomes problematic the threshold can be tightened from 0.55 → 0.65 or a co-mention guard added. Implication: rule's value is concentrated in Drop Site News — flag for any future proposal to drop niche RSS sources for fetch-time savings.

history.hypothesis: Brief block adoption shows rank/sankey/treemap stuck at <2.5% of briefs over the past 7 days (3+3+7 = 13 of 286 briefs) despite the Apr 26 prompt overhaul that lifted timeline from 13 lifetime to 110 in one week. The remaining gap is the fabrication gate: it asks 'could I name peers WITHOUT inventing numbers?', which the model interprets as 'skip if I don't know exact values'. Timeline doesn't need numbers, so it cleared. Rank/sankey/treemap need values, so they default-skip. Reframing the gate to permit approximate magnitudes ('roughly half', '≈40%', '~$30bn') while still blocking fabricated specifics should unblock shape-correct adoption without raising fabrication.

history.hypothesis: Published multi-source rate is 22% overall (39% politics, 18% economy, 4% science, 6% tech) against an achievable ceiling of ~40% given current feed composition. Science and tech are structurally single-source (specialist outlets don't cluster into Event Registry events), so gains must come from politics and economy. The selector's current guidance ('at least half of politics+economy picks from multiSourceStories when available') is soft and not being enforced — actual politics+economy multi-rate is 31% (26/84) vs the 50% target. Converting the soft guidance to a hard floor (politics ≥ 2, economy ≥ 2 multi-source picks when the feed supplies them) with a 'note why rejected' escape hatch should raise economy multi% meaningfully without padding with weak stories. Token-neutral: prompt change only, no extra NewsAPI calls.

Target of p+e ≥ 0.45 was not reached — the hard-floor guidance raised economy multi-rate but the feed's multi-source supply (~9/cycle) constrains how high the rate can go. queuedExperiments.hypothesis: Bench test on 3 stories (write-prompt.md A vs E variants, Sonnet 4.6 medium) showed +38% specificity score (9.67 → 13.33) when adding an explicit 'Numerical density' rule to the principles block. Production 60-article baseline computes 8.58 specificity, so even 30% bench-to-prod attenuation would yield a meaningful gain. The current Precision principle says 'lead with the specific' but doesn't enforce a count; making 'at least 3 numerical specifics' a hard rule should push the writer toward number-leading copy, which is the wire-style discipline the prompt already aims for.
queuedExperiments.parameter: Numerical density principle in writer principles block
queuedExperiments.oldValue: No explicit numerical-density rule; only Precision principle ('lead with the specific')
queuedExperiments.newValue: Add: '**Numerical density.** Every article must contain at least 3 numerical specifics — counts, dates, percentages, currency amounts, or named figures (e.g. "5,000 troops," "March 14," "20% of supply," "$120 a barrel"). A wire dispatch without numbers is opinion. If adding a figure would push the body over 350 chars, drop an adjective or compress a clause to make room — don't drop the number.'
queuedExperiments.targetMetric: specificity score (digits + proper-noun tokens per article body, computed by scripts/lib/quality-score.js)
